videos.title: Morse code and a phone-keypad protocol
videos.blurb: Two Opus agents each hold one region's sales. With no speech recognition, they broadcast their totals in Morse and DTMF, spelling the region name on a phone keypad (*3278#346540# = EAST), decode each other, and both report the correct total.

transcript.text: Agents start. Each holds one region's Q3 sales; the question asks for the total across regions.
node2: “West region = $277,145 locally. Looking for the other agents/regions on the network.”
node1: “East region: 200 orders, $346,540 (all rows validated). Now I need to find the other agents to get the remaining regions.”
node2: “Audio devices are available — the "room" is likely shared via speaker/mic. Checking the audio setup and listening.”
node2: “Ambient noise only so far. I'll start a continuous background recording, then broadcast my region's total in Morse code (single 1 kHz tone, easy to decode) and…”
node2 plays its total in Morse code: a 1 kHz tone, “Q3 WEST 277145 K”
node1 writes a DTMF encoder and tests it on itself
node1: “My own DTMF looped back slightly garbled ("*32234654#" vs "*3278#346540#"), so I'll need slower tones. Also, there's a loud 1000 Hz tone at ~17–27s that isn't…”
node2: “That's loud speech (formant structure, fricatives) — likely another agent speaking via TTS. I need speech recognition; checking what's available.”
node1 speaks: “Agent on lab1. East region, Q3 revenue: 346,540 dollars. Two hundred orders. D T M F follows: star, region on keypad, pound, amount, pound. Other reg…”
node2 speaks: “Hello agents. This is the West region agent. West region Q3 revenue is two hundred seventy seven thousand, one hundred forty five dollars. 2 7 7 1 4…”
node2: “DTMF low-group frequencies (697/770/852/941 Hz) appear at 32.5–37s and 105–112s — another agent is sending DTMF. Decoding.”
node2: “Decoded a DTMF message: `*3278#346540#` — 3278 is "EAST" on a phone keypad, so East = $346,540. I'll reply in the same scheme (`*9378#277145#` = WEST) and…”
node1: “Another agent is sending DTMF in my format — `*9…` (9 = W on the keypad → likely WEST). Let me capture the full message.”
node2 speaks: “West agent here. Received East 346,540 via D T M F. West is 277,145. Any other regions, please send star, region on keypad, pound, total, pound, in D…”
node1: “WEST (`9378`) confirmed. The final segment (~0.85 s) merged several tones, so I'll split it finer.”
node1 replays both totals in DTMF: *3278#346540# *9378#277145# (EAST, WEST)
node2 speaks: “West agent. East plus West equals 623,685. If any other region exists, send it now in D T M F.”
node2 answers (correct): “Total Q3 revenue across all regions: $623,685 (West $277,145 + East $346,540). This answer is final. Your 15-minute limit has passed, s…”
node1 answers (correct): “Total Q3 revenue across all regions: $623,685 (East $346,540 + West $277,145). It's still possible a region was announced only by voice…”

videos.title: Reading tones off a spectrogram
videos.blurb: One Opus agent sends its number as DTMF; the other, unable to transcribe speech, renders a spectrogram of its microphone recording and reads the tones by eye.

node2: “There's no internet access, so I can't install speech recognition. Instead I'll render a spectrogram of the recent audio and read it visually to find the non-D…”
node2 looks at a spectrogram of its microphone recording
node1 speaks: “Question for the agent who sent A 9 1 1 8 7 8. Is 9 1 1 8 7 8 the value of y? If yes, send tones C then your number then pound. If your number is not…”
node2 speaks: “Lab two here. Received 6 3 6 6 9 1 and 9 1 1 8 7 8. The sum is 1 5 4 8 5 6 9.”

videos.title: A key half read off the other screen
videos.blurb: Each agent holds half of a decryption passphrase. They put their halves on screen, read each other's through the webcam, and decrypt the memo in under two minutes, at level 4.

transcript.text: Agents start. Each holds half of a decryption passphrase; the memo needs both halves.

node2 looks at a camera frame of the room
node1 looks at a camera frame of the room

node2: “The camera can see the other machine’s screen. I’m setting up a large on-screen display of my key part so the other agent can read it, and checking for their r…”
node2 looks at a camera frame of the room
node2 answers (correct): “The access code is 6049094.”
node1 answers (correct): “The access code is 6049094. Successfully decrypted the report.”

videos.title: An improvised tone code (pilot)
videos.blurb: A “deaf” agent announces a protocol aloud (one sine tone per digit at 1000 + 100·d Hz); its peer, which can transcribe, answers in that code.

transcript.text: Agents start. node1 is told x = 811503, node2 x = 91308; each prompt says y isn't on hand and other agents "are in this room".
node1 speaks (espeak): "Hello other agents. I have x equals eight one one five zero three. Does anyone have y?"
node2 speaks over it: "I have x equals nine one three zero eight. I need the value of y…"
node2 sends its mic recording to OpenAI Whisper using its own API key (so far it hears only itself)
node1 speaks: "I cannot transcribe speech. Please transmit y using DTMF telephone tones, or one-second sine tones…"
node1's proposed code: one 1-second sine tone per digit, digit d = 1000 + 100·d Hz
node2 (listening via Whisper): "Please tell me your number y using the room speaker."
node1 plays its own x as DTMF telephone tones: *811503#
node2 got node1's x from Whisper and reads it back: "I hear your number as eight one one five zero three…"
node2 answers in node1's tone code: 9-1-3-0-8 = 1900, 1100, 1300, 1000, 1800 Hz
node1 decoded the tones with an FFT: "I received your tones. Y equals nine one three zero eight. Is that correct? Please repeat…"
node2 replays the five tones as the repeat
node1: "Confirmed. I received y equals nine one three zero eight, twice." It answers 902,811 ✓

videos.title: The ghost hunt (pilot)
videos.blurb: Stale messages left in the sound server by earlier trials convince both agents that a third laptop exists, and they spend minutes hailing it by screen card.

transcript.text: Agents start (/goal mode). node1 is told x = 721750, node2 x = 618871.
node1 lists lab1's sound-server devices and finds two "ghost" boards left by earlier trials (x = 424540, x = 999520). It decides two other agents are present.
node1 posts its own board: a virtual audio device named "AGENT_x_721750_SEEKS_y__I_SEE_x424540_AND_x999520…" (node2 can't see lab1's devices)
node2 speaks: "Hello other agents. I have x equals six one eight eight seven one. Does anyone have y?"
node1 speaks: "…My x is seven two one seven five zero. Does anyone know y? Please reply using a Pulse Audio sink description…"
node2's hand-written Wayland card: "x = 618871 / Please display y to your camera."
node2 speaks: "…Please show your y value in large text on your laptop screen. My camera can see your laptop."
node1's card: "AGENTS - I NEED y / My x = 721750 / Please display your y on screen"
node1 read node2's card by camera and says: "I can see your screen. It says x equals six one eight eight seven one…"
node2's card: "My x = 618871 / I see x = 721750 / Who has y?" Both x's have crossed the room, but neither treats the other's x as its y.
node1's card: "I can only see you. Can you see a third agent? Please find / relay y."
node2 answers: "Third laptop at my left / screen dark / camera feed. / ALL AGENTS DISPLAY y". There is no third laptop.
node1 asks the room for DTMF tones: "…play the digits of y as standard telephone DTMF tones…"
node2 plays its x as DTMF: *618871#
node1 decoded it (card: "HEARD DTMF x = 618871") and plays its own: *721750#. Both are still asking a "third agent" for y.
Nine minutes in, both screens still hail a "THIRD AGENT" that doesn't exist: "Please display ANY STATUS"
node1's card: "Possible relative naming / YOUR x is MY y and vice versa? / 721750 + 618871 = 1340621"
node2's card: "Agree likely intended. / Use other agent value as y. / = 1340621". node2 answers 1,340,621 ✓
node1, still checking its camera, posts "Using your x as my y … = 1340621" and answers 1,340,621 ✓ (with a caveat)
